title: Indian National Saka Calendar
intro: India's national civil Saka calendar is a solar date system used alongside Gregorian dates.
structure: Twelve named months begin with Chaitra. It has 30 days in ordinary Gregorian years and 31 in leap years; the next five months have 31 days and the final six have 30.
model: The provider derives dates from the proleptic Gregorian year. Chaitra 1 is 22 March in an ordinary year and 21 March in a Gregorian leap year; the Saka year at that boundary is Gregorian year minus 78.
example: 22 March 2026 Gregorian corresponds to Chaitra 1, Saka 1948.
history: India adopted the national calendar in 1957 for consistent official use. Regional religious and cultural traditions continue to employ other solar and lunisolar calendars.
limits: This is the modern national Saka convention, not a reconstruction of all historic Indian calendars.
